workbookName: Episode Dialog Copy — Craft Wave 2 (35 series)
sheetName: Craft batch 2 (BE@RBRICK, Goldie, Greatness Code, My Brother the Minotaur)

rows.story_lead: Jasmine writes songs her parents have forbidden, and the band rehearses in disguise while a pop career blooms under a fake name. Crashing the DMBEETZ concert puts the secret, and the dream, on the line. The band's own anthem says it plainly: you have the right to choose.
rows.resolution: Frustrated but brave, Jasmine stands up for herself through the music itself, claiming the choice her parents say is not hers to make.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (music video plus surprise, crashing the DMBEETZ concert)'; script-level story detail grounds the lead and resolution; confidence high. The disguised-identity workaround is a series-long thread, not resolved here.

rows.story_lead: The chorus will not come, and the band's practice space is one bake sale away from being lost. Jasmine keeps working the line until free to be me finally lands. When Ms. Goldenshorts threatens the baker's new flavors, the crowd rallies behind her.
rows.resolution: The block breaks through persistence, and the band's message of self-expression gives a baker the nerve to break from her own mold.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (unique practice space, baker breaks from the mold)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Miss Milton hides a wrestler's heart under the math teacher's job, and the newly named Brushstrokes throw her a live event to prove it. Keeping the band secret from her own parents weighs on Jasmine. The night ends with her coming clean, and with a surprise: her parents were once a musical duo.
rows.resolution: Nervousness lifts when Jasmine talks it out, and her parents respond with understanding instead of the punishment she had pictured. Miss Milton stays a teacher but makes math her own.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (math teacher longs to wrestle, band hosts the live event)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: DMBEETZ score a hit with a stolen Brushstrokes song, and the theft stings worse because the meaning got twisted. Nick's mom shares the dance dream she gave up and asks for help stepping into the spotlight. At the contest, Ms. Hazard dances her own routine.
rows.resolution: Disappointment and frustration find a place to go: the band refuses to quit, and this was never about winning becomes the family's own answer to a rigged contest.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (DMBEETZ score a hit after stealing the song, Nick's mom steps into the spotlight)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Todd promises the Brushstrokes a BRBX Media broadcast, and Klaus's mischievous parents threaten to sink it, robot piranhas included. Klaus tries so hard to be agreeable that he keeps helping the wrong people. The friends catch him before the window-breaking plan goes live.
rows.resolution: Klaus's worry about becoming what his family is gets answered out loud: trying to help and having it go wrong is an everyone thing, not a you thing.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Todd promises the broadcast, Klaus's mischievous parents threaten it)'; confidence high. Content considerations: comic villainy (robot piranhas, window-breaking plan), all resolved.

rows.story_lead: Rewriting Ms. Goldenshorts's school musical, the Brushstrokes discover Vanessa, an anxious understudy who has been told she will never be a lead. Stage fright nearly wins. Jasmine tells her the confidence is hers to find, and Vanessa returns to sing the finale.
rows.resolution: Stage fright and mean-girl undermining do not get the last word; Vanessa tries the spotlight again and takes it.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (rising star discovered while rewriting the musical)'; confidence high. Content considerations: anxiety about performing, mean-girl undermining, resolved.

rows.story_lead: A vengeful Ms. Goldenshorts vows to unmask the Brushstrokes, and every kid in class faces group punishment until someone snitches. Jasmine recruits extra help instead. Holly's third option lets no one rat and everyone declare together.
rows.resolution: The pressure to snitch dissolves into collective action, and Jasmine and Ada both apologize for doubting Holly when her plan was the way out.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Goldenshorts goes all out to unmask the band, Jasmine recruits help to keep the secret)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Jasmine cannot connect with a bandmate while Holly's parents smother her with deals and worry, and the new song is overdue. Jasmine keeps over-wording it under the deadline. She finally admits her plan and tells Holly the truth about the song.
rows.resolution: Honesty heals the fight Jasmine caused: Holly thanks her for not giving special treatment, and Holly asks her parents for space to choose for herself.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Jasmine struggles to connect with a bandmate, Holly's family makes a deal with Goldenshorts)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: The biggest stage of the band's life is hours away, and the nerves spiral through all of them. Calm breathing, art therapy and dance therapy steady them one by one. At the studio, Todd's betrayal waits, and the escape ends on a breakup announcement.
rows.resolution: Breath, paint and dance work the anxiety loose. Whatever happens, we still have each other carries the band out the door.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (major opportunity fuels anxiety, Jasmine soothes bandmates, trouble awaits at the studio)'; confidence high. Content consideration: Todd's betrayal revealed, escape ends on the breakup-announcement cliff.

rows.story_lead: The Brushstrokes plan a rooftop concert to prove they are still together, and things do not go as expected. Klaus lets Todd play bass again while saying out loud that forgiveness is not owed yet. The band follows Holly's trust me into the unknown.
rows.resolution: Old hurt sits beside new music as Klaus gives a second chance he has not finished feeling, and the trust lands just before Goldenshorts's announcement turns everything around.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (rooftop concert to prove they are still together, things do not go as expected)'; confidence high. Cliffhanger: Goldenshorts announces Holly in DMBEETZ.

rows.story_lead: Holly has been working undercover to expose DMBEETZ as robots, and the truth costs her when her parents cut the friendship off. The band finally learns the plan. Welcoming her back takes an apology and a fight worth having.
rows.resolution: Lonely and sad under the parents' ban, Holly talks it out with the band, and the apology that follows puts the friendship back where it belongs.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (a shocking twist changes everything, the band digs deep to support a friend)'; confidence high. Content consideration: parents cutting off a friendship, resolved with apology.

rows.story_lead: The rule-enforcer's own story surfaces in a journal: she once wanted exactly what these kids want, and she gave it up. Trapped in Mr. Hitmaker's studio while the DMBEETZ drama swirls, the band needs family to reach them. Holly leaves her mom an honest voicemail about the life she actually wants.
rows.resolution: Sad turns to brave when Holly tells her mother the truth, the apology that comes back is too tight but real, and the journal makes Goldenshorts a person instead of a wall.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Ms Goldenshorts deals with DMBEETZ drama, the band is trapped in the studio)'; confidence high. Content consideration: mild peril, resolved.

rows.story_lead: A town on the edge of giving up every choice out of fear gets one more show from the Brushstrokes. The kids are unmasked and believed anyway. The line for the adult who forgot her own dreams lands gently: it is also not our fault that you just gave up.
rows.resolution: Brave and worried, the band stands up for everyone's right to choose, and the town answers by painting its own destinies with them.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (race to stop Ms Goldenshorts, one more show, inspiring fans to paint their own destinies)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Goldie hunts for the perfect Gotcha Day present for her best friend Teeny, and her bigness keeps breaking the celebration she is trying to honor. Gotcha Day, the party says, is the day a person joined a family by adoption. The mess she leaves behind is spectacular.
rows.resolution: Goldie apologizes to Teeny straight away, and the friends name what actually makes her a good friend, which turns out to be none of the presents.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (perfect present for Teeny, party ruined, friends rally)'; confidence high. The Gotcha Day reveal is a warm adoption mirror.

rows.story_lead: Goldie gets stuck, and the town that usually gawks at the giant girl treats her like a spectacle instead of a neighbor. Mrs. Petunia starts charging admission. The unkindness ends when Goldie tells the town she is not a monster, and the kids ask to be her friends.
rows.resolution: Scared and embarrassed, Goldie asks for help instead of hiding, and the town's answer is friendship rather than a sideshow.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (sticky situation, friends band together)'; confidence high. Mrs. Petunia's paying-sideshow beat is a brief unkindness worth knowing. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (help-seeking story, no ratified topic fits).

rows.story_lead: Teeny is too short for the fair rides, and the height requirement comes with a side of not being taken seriously. She tries stretching, stacking and scheming to grow. Only tiny Teeny can fit the mouse maze, which makes the point better than any speech.
rows.resolution: Frustration and disappointment settle into Teeny's own conclusion, no matter what size you are you are the same person, and Goldie lets her reach it in her own time.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (too short for rides, tries to grow taller)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (fair-rides/body-size story).

rows.story_lead: Petey's imaginary friend Pilroy has gone missing, and the search is really about the growing up underneath it. Outgrowing a friend who was never visible is its own quiet goodbye. Somewhere in the hunt, a sharp word lands wrong between friends.
rows.resolution: The hurt feelings get an apology, and the imaginary friend gets a send-off that leaves the door open.
rows.evidence_note: Script-tier set per the batch sheet, but this row's note field is a PLACEHOLDER with no per-row script verification statement. Lead and resolution built from the row's situation, emotion and coping tags plus the episode synopsis; confidence low-medium.

rows.story_lead: Hide-and-seek is hard when you are the only giant in town, and Goldie loses every round to bushes that fit everyone else. She says the quiet part out loud: being the only one her size makes her feel alone. Her friends answer with the giant perks they love, list included.
rows.resolution: The loneliness eases because Goldie names the feeling out loud, and the naming gets answered with belonging instead of empty reassurance.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (hide-and-seek she cannot play like friends, creative hiding spot)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Everyone fawns over Goldie's Hand, the giant helper that opens jars and doors, and Goldie is jealous of her own hand. She also cannot fit inside Teeny's house for the sleepover everyone else is enjoying. The two friends talk it through and admit they gave up too fast on a party that works for every size.
rows.resolution: Jealousy and sadness get said plainly, Teeny answers that we like Hand because it is part of you, and the party gets rebuilt for everyone.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (cannot fit inside Teeny's house for a sleepover, gets creative)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (jealousy/sleepover story).

rows.story_lead: Goldie appoints herself a friendship matchmaker and pairs off everyone in town by force. The pairs clash over identical outfits and opposite opinions, and the plan collapses loudly. She owns it in her own words: you cannot force friendship.
rows.resolution: Embarrassed and sad about the wreckage, Goldie apologizes to the pairs she engineered, and Mrs. Petunia's contentment alone makes a gentle counterpoint.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (works hard to find a best friend for everyone)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (friendship-engineering story).

rows.story_lead: Teeny takes the mayor's chair for a day, and the job buries her by lunch. The ribbon cutting gets missed, the zone P paperwork goes sideways, and the broken playground waits. Goldie and Romeo quietly finish the repair overnight so the job can be about play again.
rows.resolution: The overwhelm and impatience end when Teeny asks for help, and the mayor rediscovers that play was the job all along.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Teeny steps into an important job for the day)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (responsibility/playground-repair story).

rows.story_lead: Inspired by Teeny's new cat, Goldie adopts a ladybug and loves it straight into a jar. Neighbor cat Juniper comes and goes through the pet door, modeling the freedom part. The mistake is Goldie's to see.
rows.resolution: Goldie apologizes to the ladybug directly and learns that loving something and holding it too tight are different sizes of the same feeling.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (inspired by Teeny's cat adoption, Goldie looks for a pet of her own)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: A rumored dinosaur has Boysenberg panicking before the Boysenween costume fun even starts. Nobody has actually seen it. The song spells the cure: pause, think, consider the facts, breathe, relax.
rows.resolution: The town's scare dissolves with a few deep breaths, and the monster turns out to be Goldie in a half-finished costume.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (costume for the magical springtime holiday, town panic)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: An accident wrecks Mrs. Petunia's home, and the house hunt lands her in Goldie's nest, where both tempers rub wrong. Give and take takes practice. Petunia admits she is new to kindness given for nothing.
rows.resolution: The friction eases with patience on both sides, and the give-and-take song carries the lesson without preaching.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Mrs. Petunia searches for a new home, ends up in Goldie's nest)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (making-amends story).

rows.story_lead: Petey has stopped believing in aliens, and Goldie cannot bear it. Her own outgrown fairy stars motivate a well-meant trick to bring the magic back. Caught, she confesses, and Petey's answer is better than the trick: with friends like you, anything is possible.
rows.resolution: Goldie's sadness about lost magic gets an honest apology instead of a successful scheme, and the wonder comes back on its own.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Petey stops believing in aliens, Goldie tries to reignite the magic)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Goldie joins the choir and starts shrinking her voice so a friend will not be overshadowed. The truth only comes out at rehearsal. The mayor settles it so both voices are heard as they are, and his line is the keeper: never make yourself littler for me.
rows.resolution: Nervous and embarrassed, Goldie talks it out instead of singing small, and the choir learns two full voices can share one song.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Goldie joins the choir but worries she is too loud)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: An egg appears in Goldie's nest, and egg-sitting turns out to be the most patient job in Boysenberg. She leaves with a decoy once, and the mistake costs her. The long wait pays off when the hatched pegamoose reunites with its mother.
rows.resolution: The guilt of the decoy mistake turns into patience, and the patience is what brings mother and chick back together.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (finding an egg in her nest, does her best to care for it)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (egg-sitting care story).

rows.story_lead: Super Goldie flies into action, and the town keeps casting her as the boulder or the monster because of her size. Her rescues misfire, including a cat that had just found its own courage. The friends apologize for casting by appearance and name her real-life hero moments instead.
rows.resolution: The frustration of being seen wrong gets answered out loud, and Goldie's egg-sitting patience and Petunia nestmate stay count as the heroism they are.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (flies into action as her new heroic persona)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (superhero-play identity story).

rows.story_lead: A cuddly new pal feels everything as big as Goldie does, and the town is not ready for two of them. Goldie asks Wooly to be quieter, then hears her own mistake in the request. She owns it one giant to another.
rows.resolution: The loneliness of feeling too much for the room ends with an apology, one giant to another, and the friends confirm the waterworks are among the things they love about her.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (a cuddly pal shares the same big feelings as Goldie)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (big-feelings friendship story).

rows.story_lead: Teeny invents a game, and the rulebook grows until nobody is having any fun. A fantasy sequence crowns her a king dethroned for over-ruling. She names the problem herself and lets the friends choose their own way to play.
rows.resolution: Teeny's disappointment turns into naming the feeling, no one is having any fun, and the game survives by losing half its rules.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Teeny creates a game that might have too many rules)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: A nightmare convinces Goldie that her own bigness is a danger to the people she loves, and she starts keeping her friends at a distance. Petey states it plainly: using a wheelchair does not mean he cannot take care of himself. Then he saves her at the clock tower.
rows.resolution: The scary dream loses its grip because Goldie talks it out, and the trust she learns at the clock tower does the rest.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Goldie has a nightmare and faces a new fear)'; confidence high. Content consideration handled in the source: Petey's wheelchair line is stated plainly, resolution is trust not reassurance alone.

rows.story_lead: Goldie wants to try the new skates, and the taller you are, the farther you fall. Her friends build a giant pair just for her, and the town makes falling safe so trying is too. Mrs. Petunia, an expert biker, wobbles onto skates for the first time herself.
rows.resolution: The fear of falling loses to trying again, and Petunia proves it is never too late to be a beginner.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (friends team up to build a giant pair of roller skates)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Goldie travels back in time to erase one embarrassing moment, and the past has opinions. Helping the young mayor through his own first-day blunders becomes the mirror she needed. Nobody in the future, she realizes, has ever mentioned his flub once.
rows.resolution: The embarrassment shrinks once Goldie reframes it: everyone's most cringe-worthy moment is also the one no one else remembers.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (travels back in time to undo an embarrassing moment)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: The mayor's dinner party is coming, and Goldie is sure she is not fancy enough. Petey and Teeny coach her in opposite directions until she can barely recognize herself. The mayor wanted the funny, generous, giant-hearted girl everyone loves all along.
rows.resolution: Goldie's nerves and the changing-to-fit-in trap end when she talks it out, and the host asks for the guest she already was.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (worries she is not fancy enough as the dinner approaches)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (fitting-in/dinner-party story).

rows.story_lead: Romeo is away, and Goldie is on her own for the first time. She pretends she is fine until she cannot pour the honey, mind the nest and smile at once. The admission finally comes: I can not do anything.
rows.resolution: Once Goldie asks for help, the friends descend on the chores, and Romeo confesses he needed her help on his trip too, so the alone feeling was never one-sided.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (struggles to take care of herself while Romeo is away)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (first-time-alone story).

rows.story_lead: The tooth fairy leaves Goldie a treasure, and she spends it on everything except the town's cracked problem. The giant potato fiasco that follows is her teacher. She says the regret out loud: she should have fixed the crack first.
rows.resolution: The disappointment of wanting everything turns into asking for help, the town mashes the potato together, and the mayor closes with take care of each other.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (the tooth fairy leaves a special surprise)'; confidence high. Coping judgment call from dev set: the fix is collective, and asking for help is the nearest term.

rows.story_lead: Wooly has tough news to share, and the word is moving. Goldie cries a flood, and the town deploys canoes, because the Goldie Guide treats the crying as feeling, not fault. Wooly's own reframe does the soft landing: the friendship is changing into a different kind of special thing.
rows.resolution: The goodbye sadness gets asked-for comfort instead of hushing, and a postcard one week later seals the friendship as something that travels.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Goldie feels sad when Wooly shares tough news)'; confidence high. Topics note from dev set: none defensible (friend-moving-away story).

rows.story_lead: Goldie and Romeo's catchy new tune sweeps Boysenberg, and suddenly Romeo is the star while Goldie watches from the crowd. He stays quiet to protect her fun, which is its own kind of problem. Mrs. Petunia's manager ambitions crank the pressure.
rows.resolution: Loneliness in the spotlight's shadow pushes Goldie to stand up for herself, and the duet is restored as the better fun because anyone can be a star.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (a catchy new tune sweeps Boysenberg)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: The first snow ever lands on Boysenberg, and nothing about the party goes as planned. Mrs. Petunia hoards marshmallows and sticks to her expert plan while the fun happens without her. She arrives with cocoa at the end, which is its own quiet turn.
rows.resolution: The frustration of a ruined plan melts once Goldie lets the day change shape, and even Petunia learns to share the marshmallows.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (a frosty surprise sparks major excitement)'; confidence high. Brussels sprouts roasting is the running gag; topics note from dev set: none defensible (snow and winter not in the ratified topic set).

rows.story_lead: Game 6 of the 2012 Eastern Conference Finals, in Boston, and the noise is the loudest thing in the building. LeBron James tells the story of learning to feel nothing on the court while the crowd buries him alive. I know who I am is how he describes what came after.
rows.resolution: The worry and the heckling lose to a reframe: the noise gets tuned out until the game itself is the only voice left.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (2012 Eastern Conference Finals, game 6 in Boston)'; confidence high. Content considerations: bleeped strong language, hostile crowd chatter including racist hostility in Boston and a bury-him-alive heckle.

rows.story_lead: Tom Brady has played twenty years of pro football and calls exactly one game perfect, and it is not the one you are thinking. The game no one remembers as his greatest is the one he savors. The thirst that can never be quenched is his own phrase for the striving.
rows.resolution: Pride and joy sit side by side as Brady lives fully inside the one game he calls perfect, and the trying again never stops, even at the top.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (the one perfect game, and it is not the game people think)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Alex Morgan was cut, then benched, then became the starter her coach said she had to earn. Coach Pia's earn-it lineup is the structure Morgan credits for the rise. Fear, she says, is something to take straight on.
rows.resolution: She takes fear straight on, and the trying again after failure earns the starting spot the coach demanded.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (bench player to starter on the USWNT after a dominating performance)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: The fastest man alive traces the race that told him he was born to run, 9.58 seconds in Berlin. The calm is technical: clear your mind and just listen for the gun. His Michael Johnson story closes the loop on knowing when a dream is finished.
rows.resolution: The calm is the point. Confidence and happiness do the work, and a clear mind at the start line is a move any kid can borrow before a big moment.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (the race that made him realize he was born to run, 9.58 in Berlin)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Two falls at the 2018 Olympic qualifier leave Shaun White rattled with the Games on the line. Clouds like Mordor hang over the final run. His pressure formula, total focus plus a slight bit of not caring, frees the run that follows.
rows.resolution: He stopped gripping, the worry became a reframe, and the final run landed.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (rocky qualifier performance left him rattled, then propelled him)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Katie Ledecky was an underdog teenager who just wanted to make the team, and the roar in the pool is for someone else. Her coach's reframe is the calming move: that noise is all shooting straight down your lane. Her grandpa's advice, take the lead and keep it, closes it.
rows.resolution: Swimming in someone else's crowd, Ledecky turns nerves into pride, one lap at a time.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (underdog teenager who just wanted to make the team, dominant Olympic performance)'; confidence high. The family email about podium visits is a charming beat from the script.

rows.story_lead: Kelly Slater's fifth world surfing championship arrives as a spiritual odyssey, and the biggest feelings hit right before the heat. Friend Tom Carroll talks him through ten minutes of yoga breathing on the beach. Slater also admits that wanting time off cost him heats along the way.
rows.resolution: Breath borrowed from a friend meets the pre-heat panic, and the championship follows the calm.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (fifth world surfing championship as a spiritual odyssey)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: Marcus Rashford's Manchester United debut arrives because injuries emptied the lineup, and he is ready. Years of preparation plus one instruction, stay between the width of the goals, is the entire mechanism. His home was small and the streets nearby were unsafe, and he tells it with dignity.
rows.resolution: The nerves of a sudden big chance meet pride, and the years of trying again are what made ready possible.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (injuries left the lineup short, Rashford rose to the occasion)'; confidence high. Coping judgment call from dev set: mechanism is preparation plus taking instruction, so trying again is the nearest ratified term.

rows.story_lead: Russell Wilson plays the game of his career against the Steelers with a flu that nearly sidelines him, six IVs deep. His father's question, why not you, carries the weight. The eulogy built on hash marks is where the story really lives.
rows.resolution: Wilson plays through doubt and fever both, and belief answers the doubt in his father's own words.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (career-best passing while battling a flu that nearly sidelined him)'; confidence high. Content consideration: he plays through serious illness with six IVs total, an intensity worth a parent knowing.

rows.story_lead: Leticia Bufoni wins gold at the 2015 SLS World Championship after haters said she had quit skating, and she is the only girl at the park doing it. Up by an easy score, she refuses the safe trick and lands the 360 flip she wants to win with. The early costs were real: a father who broke her board in half, neighbors who jeered at her clothes.
rows.resolution: Sadness at being doubted turns to bravery in the trick choice itself, and proving the critics wrong happens by skating exactly her way.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (2015 SLS gold, critics proved wrong, history made)'; confidence high. Content considerations: father breaking her early board, neighbor name-calling, and the ESPN Body Issue shoot (she appears nude) that drew sellout accusations.

rows.story_lead: Scout Bassett's 2017 World Para Athletics Championships are a step in a longer mental health journey, and she does not hide the visible difference on her leg. An infant fire, abandonment and orphanage years are part of the story she tells. A year and a half of therapy and medication is the help that worked.
rows.resolution: Asking for help does what powering through could not, and her line stands: I am never going to be ashamed of my story.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (2017 World Para Athletics Championships as a cathartic mental-health step)'; confidence high. Content considerations, weighty but central: infant fire, abandonment, orphanage years, depression treated with therapy and medication.

rows.story_lead: Bubba Wallace rolls into Talladega on a winless streak he describes as zero for a hundred and something, a really dark place. He becomes the first Black driver to win a NASCAR Cup Series race in 60 years. The antidote he names is the unknown of next weekend.
rows.resolution: Trying again outlasts the dark place, and the next weekend's unknown turns out to be history.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (first Black Cup winner at Talladega in 60 years)'; confidence high. Content considerations: one bleeped-adjacent hell, real crash footage, and a candid bit about fudged birth certificates to race older kids at 12 and 13.

rows.story_lead: Lindsey Vonn's grandfather, who watched every race, dies days before the Olympics, and she sprinkles his ashes on the mountain. Her greatest performance does not end in victory. Greatness is not perfection but grit and overcoming, she says, in her own closing words.
rows.resolution: Grief and pride share the podium as Vonn gives everything while not at her best, and the run itself becomes the tribute.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (greatest performance did not end in victory)'; confidence high. Content considerations: grandfather's death days before the Olympics, ashes on the mountain, career-long injury toll.

rows.story_lead: Lorcan's visions start showing up in public, and the town that raised him starts looking at him like a problem. His human brother Charlie pulls an all-night stakeout to get to the bottom of it, because you are not a case, you are my brother. A vandal spree and a classmate's story make everything worse before it gets better.
rows.resolution: Scared and confused, Lorcan talks it out with the one person who treats the mystery as his own, and the brothers start hunting for answers instead of hiding them.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (visions and acting out, human brother Charlie helps him get to the bottom of it)'; confidence high. Content considerations: the town turns on Lorcan after a vandal spree, a classmate claims the creature tried to kill him, and the adoption backstory (baby minotaur found in the woods, raised by humans) is the series spine.

rows.story_lead: A letter about Lorcan's past says raise my boy as your own, let him believe his parents are dead, and he reads it before anyone can soften it. She did not want me is the wound, and the adults' loving lie is exposed as a lie all the same. Meanwhile the Elders are trying to stop Craignelder's greedy mining plan.
rows.resolution: The confusion and sadness of being deceived get somewhere to go when Lorcan asks for help instead of swallowing the letter alone, and the honest version of his story starts here.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (elders vs Craignelder's greedy mining plan, kids uncover a link to the past)'; confidence high. Content considerations: the letter's wording is quoted in the source note, the elders are loving but concretely deceiving him, which the show plays straight.

rows.story_lead: Craignelder talks his own conflicted son into framing Lorcan for trouble he did not cause. What if it had been you who got hurt, Lorcan says out loud, and briefly quits the quest over it. Stolen pets shipping to the mainland raise the stakes beyond reputations.
rows.resolution: The fear of hurting the friends he loves gets named, and naming it is what reopens the quest when the aerial labyrinth photo appears.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (ruins exploration with hidden dangers, Craignelder enlists conflicted son to frame Lorcan)'; confidence high. Content considerations: pets are stolen and shipped to the mainland, played for plot but distressing for pet-loving kids.

rows.story_lead: Craignelder hands Lorcan a muzzle and claims his birth parents threw him away, and Lorcan shoves him in rage in front of everyone. George's lesson lands after: defend yourself and fight are a big difference. The doll reveal, a minotaur mother who made her son's favorite toy, answers the cruelest claim.
rows.resolution: Regret over the shove sits next to the anger that caused it, and the reframing comes from a handmade doll: hardly the actions of someone who did not care.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (close encounter with the Pooka leads the crew to a mysterious door)'; confidence high. Content considerations: dehumanizing muzzle gift, the shove, episode ends unresolved in the garage, which the serial earns.

rows.story_lead: George takes Lorcan to a martial arts retreat to work on the temper, and the river will not teach him until the meditation does: empty your mind, close your eyes and breathe. Back home, some in town suggest he move to the bay. His friends are meanwhile closing in on the amulet in the ruins.
rows.resolution: A calm-down practice finally meets the public anger and the exile whispers, and the breathing exercise is what Lorcan reaches for the next time the anger comes.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (martial arts retreat to help Lorcan control his anger, others uncover their biggest lead)'; confidence high.

rows.story_lead: The kids trap the Pooka with a salt ring and a plan, and Craignelder simply steps out of it. How could I have been so wrong, Charlie admits, and eats the quest-ending edict on screen. Chief Walker does the real work, confronting Craignelder and recovering the pets from Wesley's room.
rows.resolution: Embarrassment and disappointment get owned out loud, and the adults who listened fix what the trap could not.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (kids discover the Pooka's true identity and plan to catch him once and for all)'; confidence high. The Pooka's true identity is still open at episode's end.

rows.story_lead: The Elders finally explain why Lorcan was sent away: she was not abandoning him, she was saving his life. The kids' reaction, we cannot trust anybody, is played fair. The lore underneath involves a war between worlds and a king who rejected his own weak newborn.
rows.resolution: The betrayal of a lifetime of secrets eases when Lorcan talks it out with the Elders, and the protection story replaces the rejection story he had built.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (Elders reveal their knowledge hoping to discourage him from going back)'; confidence high. Content considerations: war-between-worlds lore, a mind-twisting dark parasite, a king who rejected his weak newborn.

rows.story_lead: The Pooka tells Lorcan exactly what he wants to hear, you must do this alone, and the show flags it as the classic isolation move. Lorcan walks through the door and is caught, cliffhanger included. Wesley and Craignelder's fake tourist article escalates the exposure danger in parallel.
rows.resolution: Confused and scared, Lorcan learns the lonely-road pitch is the trap itself, and the friends racing to find him are the answer he could not see.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis (the Pooka lures Lorcan toward the minotaur world with false promises while the others search)'; confidence high. Ends on a cliffhanger.

rows.story_lead: Lorcan is gone, the amulet is gone, and the grown-ups say wait and hope. Charlie barely leaves his room until a dream message and a star-map breakthrough put him back in motion. The rescue takes solving, not strength, and it costs: Lorcan's minotaur father is confirmed lost in battle and his mother Arianys is wounded in the escape.
rows.resolution: Sad but determined, Charlie leads the second-gateway rescue with George, and not giving up on someone you love gets him back at any cost, exactly as promised.
rows.evidence_note: Script: dev set row note reads 'script; identity verified vs synopsis'; confidence high. Content considerations: Lorcan captured by minotaur soldiers, father confirmed lost in battle, Arianys wounded in the escape.

rows.story_lead: Dark forces infiltrate Bryony Island, and the temptation speaks straight to Lorcan's belonging wound: join us and you will finally fit. His sister Kai acts under its control, and Chief Walker's fairy-guardian reveal lands mid-battle. The season ends with Lorcan and Charlie walking back through the door together.
rows.resolution: Brave and proud, Lorcan stands up for himself by choosing his own world, and the brothers come home side by side.
